measured: decisive core-count sweep: writer_issue 4337 ns/8 writes at 64 cores (542 ns/call) vs 545 ns/8 writes at 1 core (68 ns/call) = 8x collapse. The 546 ns/call is FABRIC BACK-PRESSURE, not RISC command programming.
note: set_state_naive is INCORRECT: ncrisc_noc_write_with_state never reprograms NOC_RET_ADDR_COORDINATE, so every page after the first goes to the wrong DRAM bank. coord_reuse_raw is a reproduced +16..24% regression on [1,1,32,32768]. Also: interleaved DRAM TensorAccessor already uses a magic-multiply reciprocal, not a software divide - the premise that addrgen costs a divide was wrong.

decisive: writer_issue at fixed per-core payload: 4 cores 643 ns -> 64 cores 4154 ns. The store is DRAM-bandwidth-bound, not issue-bound, so a second RISC-V adds traffic to a saturated resource.
secondary_finding: NoC direction asymmetry confirmed on this op: reads on NoC1 cost 2.3x reads on NoC0; writes on NoC0 cost 4.9x writes on NoC1 - matches the noc_placement catalog entry.

domain: state_grouped +18..25% on every shape. recurrence: -4.6% on [1,1,16384,32] only, +0.3..3.9% (noise) elsewhere.
note: 12 banks is not a power of two, so 32 consecutive stick reads visit each bank only ~2.7 times - most set_state calls pay full price and the grouping bookkeeping is pure added cost.

mechanism: page->bank is page_id % num_banks (12). On every R==1 geometry every core shares start_page, so the helper ascending stick loop puts all 64 cores on the SAME bank at the same instant for 32 steps. Rotating the issue order per core is free: all 32 reads sit behind one barrier and each lands at its own L1 offset, so the block is bit-identical.
isolated_win: -17.5% mean / -18.8% max vs baseline; the raw-ascending CONTROL is flat, so the win is the rotation and not the helper bypass
domain: WIN on every total-lockstep (R==1) geometry; FLAT on partial and no-lockstep geometries; no measured regression anywhere; bit-identical everywhere

key_finding: writer_wait_out is 61-72% of the BRISC span on EVERY shape, so the issue window rotation can touch is only 15-25% of the writer stage. Rotation is a MEAN effect, not a tail effect - the 1.28x tail is unchanged or slightly worse.
structural_ceiling: a block write SET of banks is fixed by page_base and block_width_tiles; issue order changes only WHEN, never WHICH. A host-side block-id -> core permutation would change the sets and is the stronger lever (round 2 candidate).
